title: EXP-043 — Hello World Part 2: Create and Recover One FX_ IDO Property Class
objective: In the authenticated DEM configuration, use the existing IDO Property Classes runtime Form, opened through the supported Select Form route, to create exactly one tenant-wide factory-owned property class named FX_UMBase. Configure Data Type=String, Length=10, Column Data Type=the NVARCHAR option exactly as displayed in the current UI, and Label String ID=FX_sUM as a reference only. Before mutation, establish through supported Filter-in-Place queries that neither FX_UMBase nor any FX_UM-prefixed property class already exists. Perform exactly one explicit Save, verify the resulting record, ordinarily close the IDO Property Classes Form, reopen it once, and run a supported query that recovers FX_UMBase with all four attributes unchanged. Record screenshots, accessibility snapshots, operation counts, limitations, and the new class's cleanup ownership. Classification is observed only.

in_scope: Before browser actions, read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt2.md at 02:18–04:08, EXP-042-R3, and their relevant decisive evidence.

Use the existing authenticated DEM configuration G6R8LJ9Q4E8C2Z8Y_MONGOOSE_DEM_DEFAULT and Site Developer context. Editing scope is User for the surrounding factory workflow; the new property class itself is shared tenant-wide metadata.

Preflight the current browser and Web Client state. Verify the authenticated configuration, absence of obstructing dialogs, and that the target maintenance Form is not already open with uncommitted changes. Preserve unrelated Form tabs and existing data.
Open the existing IDO Property Classes runtime Form using Web Client Select Form. Do not add an Explorer shortcut or change personal settings.
Use the verified Select Form Name-filter procedure where typing is required: native Control+a, clear, then individual key-event typing. Do not bulk-fill this particular filter.

Identify the Class Name field and other runtime inputs through visible field labels and accessibility information. If a field is uncaptioned or ambiguous, use Edit > Find Value in Collection read-only, recording its property selection and closing with a freshly verified Cancel. Stop if field identity remains ambiguous.

Before creating anything, use supported Filter-in-Place queries to check exact FX_UMBase and the FX_UM prefix, including case-insensitive collisions where the supported UI permits. Capture the criteria, settled query results, and relevant count or status. Establish a working positive control using a known-existing property class without changing it. Stop if any FX_UM-prefixed class already exists or the absence check is inconclusive.
Use the native toolbar New exactly once after the collision gate passes. Verify that the intended new-record state is active and no existing record has been selected for modification.
Set Class Name to exactly FX_UMBase, Data Type to String, Length to 10, and Label String ID to exactly FX_sUM.

For Column Data Type, inspect the supported dropdown or lookup and select the actual NVARCHAR entry. A supported prefix filter in the lookup is permitted. Record the exact displayed option text and selected value; do not assume its capitalization or silently substitute another type.

For ordinary text and combobox inputs, use one plain fill without slowly, then one Tab to commit the value. Obtain a fresh snapshot and verify each value before moving to the next field. Use the supported visible dropdown selection where a combobox requires selection rather than free text.
Capture the fully configured new record before Save, including Class Name, Data Type, Length, Column Data Type and Label String ID.
Perform exactly one explicit runtime toolbar Save after verifying all attributes, using a fresh accessibility snapshot to identify the enabled Save control.
Capture the exact Save response, validation messages or absence thereof, resulting Save state, and displayed class attributes. Do not retry an uncertain Save.
Use a supported read-only collection query after Save to retrieve exactly FX_UMBase and verify its four configured attributes.

Close the clean IDO Property Classes Form through its ordinary Form-tab close control exactly once. Reopen it once through Select Form and perform a supported exact-name query. Compare all recovered attributes with the post-Save baseline.
Permit one dismissal of an obstructing portal notification using only its freshly verified close x control. Never open its links.

Before responding to any prompt or alert, obtain a fresh snapshot and verify the exact accessible button label and reference. Stop on unexpected validation, overwrite, discard or ambiguous confirmation prompts.
Allow at most one fresh recovery snapshot and one corrected visible inspection after an interaction failure. Stop if the required postcondition remains unverified.
Capture decisive screenshots and accessibility snapshots under evidence/EXP-043/ that visibly establish target identity, query criteria, creation state, Save result, and recovered attribute values.
Record the created FX_UMBase property class in evidence/EXP-043/cleanup-inventory.md, including its shared scope, exact attributes, cleanup ownership, and whether any cleanup was performed.

Confine repository edits to the EXP-043 experiment record and evidence/EXP-043/. Record a final acceptance matrix, operation counts, recovery accounting, repository-confinement audit, and final browser state.

artifacts: FX_UMBase — exactly one new tenant-wide IDO property class, created and verified through the existing IDO Property Classes runtime Form
FX_sUM — Label String ID reference only; no string resource creation

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight screenshots and accessibility snapshots establish the authenticated DEM configuration and usable Web Client. The existing IDO Property Classes Form is identified through Select Form, with no unintended Form or preference changes. Repository baseline and intended tenant-wide object scope are documented.

Before mutation, supported Filter-in-Place evidence establishes zero existing FX_UMBase and zero FX_UM-prefixed property classes in the queried collection, including case-insensitive collisions where supported. A known-existing property class is recovered as a positive control. Any collision or inconclusive query fails the creation gate.

Exactly one native New action opens a new property-class record. Evidence identifies the relevant runtime fields by labels or verified property mappings, with no existing class selected for modification.

Before Save, screenshots and accessibility snapshots identify the new Class Name as FX_UMBase, Data Type as String, Length as 10, Label String ID as FX_sUM, and Column Data Type as the UI-selected NVARCHAR option. The exact displayed Column Data Type label is recorded. No other property class is changed.

Exactly one explicit runtime Save is recorded after the attributes have been verified. The response and settled UI show successful completion without validation, duplicate-name, or unexpected confirmation errors. No Save retry or additional mutation occurs.

One supported post-Save read-only exact-name query returns exactly one FX_UMBase class with String, Length 10, the recorded NVARCHAR Column Data Type, and Label String ID FX_sUM. Evidence captures the full attributes and class identity, not merely a selected grid row.
Exactly one ordinary close of the clean IDO Property Classes Form completes without a save-changes or discard prompt. A screenshot or snapshot confirms the Form tab is removed.

One supported Select Form reopen followed by one exact-name collection query recovers exactly one FX_UMBase with every recorded attribute identical to the AC-6 baseline, no unexpected rows, and no error. This establishes observed same-session Web Client recovery only.

The cleanup inventory records exactly one created FX_UMBase class, its four attributes, the FX_sUM reference, shared tenant-wide scope, cleanup ownership, and no deletion. The final experiment record reconciles the acceptance checks with inspected evidence, operation counts, error and recovery accounting, repository confinement, and final browser state. All findings remain observed rather than replay_verified.

initial_instruction: T1 — READ-ONLY PREFLIGHT AND COLLISION GATE ONLY. Read AGENTS.md, the Hello World Part 2 transcript section 02:18–04:08, EXP-042-R3 and its decisive evidence. Confirm the authenticated DEM Web Client and record the repository baseline. Using the supported Select Form route, identify and open the existing IDO Property Classes runtime Form without altering Explorer shortcuts or User Preferences. Identify the Class Name filtering field. Use supported Filter-in-Place queries and a known-existing positive control to establish whether any FX_UM-prefixed class, including FX_UMBase, already exists. Capture settled screenshots and accessibility snapshots showing the exact query criteria, Form identity and result. Stop if a collision is found or the absence gate cannot be proven. Do not invoke New, enter a class definition, or Save in T1. Do not change another property class or perform any cache, metadata, source-control or deployment operation. A portal notification may be dismissed once using its freshly verified close x. Use no browser JavaScript. Keep recovery to one fresh snapshot and one corrected visible inspection, then stop if unresolved. Document the outcome under EXP-043 only and leave the runtime clean for operator review before the creation step.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261010-173904-H4L5. Rationale: EXP-042-R3 established an observed Web Client procedure for field identification, controlled runtime data entry, a single Save, complete collection queries, and same-session recovery after ordinary Form close/reopen. The next smallest step in Hello World Part 2 is to create one reusable IDO property class using the existing IDO Property Classes runtime Form. This introduces one new metadata-object category without changing the established FX_HelloWorld01 table, IDO, Form, or test records. Because an IDO property class is shared metadata rather than a User-scoped Form definition, collision prevention and confinement to exactly one FX_-prefixed class are mandatory. This experiment tests class creation and same-session recovery only, not downstream class visibility in the IDO wizard. | Operator review: exact-value guard (FX_UMBase, FX_sUM) and no-JavaScript policy added. Approved by the operator 2026-10-10.
